newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha little moved amid lack of incentives.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha little moved amid lack of incentives.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were stable to a little firmer in afternoon trade on Wedneday amid a lack of fresh incentives from overseas, traders said.

The backwardation in naphtha's inter-month spreads, which had narrowed by 50 cents to $1.00 on Tuesday from Monday's levels, was squeezed further with arbitrage cargoes from Europe putting downward pressure on near-term cargoes, they added.
The one-month spread from second-half May was discussed at plus $1.50/2.50 in Wednesday trading.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half May was assessed at $224.00/225.00 per tonne, compared to Tuesday's $223.00/224.50.
First-half June was notionally quoted at $223.00/224.50.
In Tuesday dealing, second half June was sold by a Singapore trader to a European trading house at $222.50. It was traded again later on the day at $222.00.
The arbitrage cargoes from Europe is expected to total as much as 400,000 tonnes with arrival dates ranging from early April to mid-May, traders said.
About half of the cargoes were destined for Asia for short-covering, while the other half remanined on the shelf for sale, they added.
